To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• eSET policy should be adopted in all UK centres • eSET policy must be linked to the ability to cryo preserve and thaw any remaining quality embryos • a maximum number of embryos to be transferred in a double embryo transfer should be 2 • a maximum number to be transferred in triple embryo transfer should be three • a maximum number for fresh blastocyst transfer should be 1.

the use of eSET has resulted in a decrease in the incidence of twins, a decrease in the perinatal mortality rate, an increase in the live birth rate, a decrease in multiple births, and an improvement in the cost-effectiveness of IVF.
• eSET is safe and effective • eSET reduces multiple pregnancies • eSET reduces perinatal morbidity and maternal morbidity

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is sufficient to support an eSET policy for patients undergoing IVF/ICSI treatment.
eSET is safe and is associated with a reduction in the rate of multiple pregnancies and should be offered to all women undergoing IVF treatment.
the evidence is sufficient to recommend an eSET policy for all women under 40 years, and that the evidence is insufficient to recommend eSET policy for women 40 years and above.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that eSET in women with a good prognosis is a safe procedure and that the use of eSET can significantly reduce the number of twin pregnancies without compromising the live birth rate.

the use of an eSET strategy in IVF/ICSI cycles with a single good embryo is a safe and effective way to reduce multiple pregnancies and their associated morbidity and mortality without compromising the chances of achieving a live birth.

the introduction of an elective single policy is associated with a reduction in the incidence of multiple pregnancies and a reduction in multiple birth rate, without compromising the chances of live birth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of elective single embryo transfer (eSET) is a safe and effective way to reduce the rate of multiple pregnancies and births without compromising the chances of achieving pregnancy or the birth of a healthy baby.
the number of embryos transferred should be limited to the minimum necessary to maximize the chances of a successful pregnancy.
the number of embryos transferred should be based on the age of the woman, her ovarian reserve, and her previous reproductive history, rather than the number of available embryos.
